title: CLO Technique Mini-Class - Adjusting the Strap Through a D-Ring Buckle
description: CLO technical experts guide you to use attachments to simulate the real adjustment belt with a Japanese-style buckle effect, suitable for any garment design.
transcript:
How to Make a Strap That Can Be Worn All Day

Hello everyone, in this technique tutorial class,  
I will introduce how to make a strap that can be worn all day.  
I believe that when you are making 3D clothing,  
you may encounter styles that require adding a strap,  
for example, the shoulder strap of a belt skirt, the shoulder strap of underwear, or the belt of clothing.  

Taking this underwear as an example:  
In the shoulder strap part of the underwear,  
an adjustment buckle called a 日字扣 (ri zi buckle) is usually used.  
We can see that the right side of this underwear has the adjustment buckle effect applied,  
while the left side shows a shoulder strap that is sewn directly.  

So how do we create a real 日字扣 effect on the shoulder strap on the right side?  
We can use the attached model.  

There is an interaction effect between the shoulder strap and the accessory that can create a realistic  
effect of the shoulder strap wearing the 日字扣.  

The current accessory model can only be used in CPU simulation,  
so we need to switch to CPU simulation here.  

Next, we take the shoulder strap on the left  
and also create a 日字扣 wearing effect.  

First, make a twist on the shoulder strap.  
We need to delete the sewing line between the shoulder strap parts,  
then use the hook and loop tool  
to hook the shoulder strap onto the strap itself.  

At the same time, we need to adjust the fabric of this shoulder strap,  
its sample shoulder strap,  
and the collision thickness.  

After adjusting these values,  
you can add this shoulder strap to the sewing line.  

Then select it in the 3D window,  
right-click to add it to the inside.  

Switching the view, you will see that this shoulder strap is now just added to the inside.  

Start the simulation.  

To prevent the shoulder strap from misaligning during simulation,  
you can add a row of fixed pins on one side of the panel.  

Switch the tool to the fixed pin,  
then add a row of fixed pins to the double-sided mouse in the center of the outside of the panel.  

Next, add a ring component.  
We can find the corresponding ring component in the accessory library.  
You can also select the component type in Connect,  
enter the component name, and search.  

Here, we can copy the existing ring component from the current project file,  
then drag it into the 3D window to add it.  

At this point, select the component,  
use the symbol in the upper right corner of the component  
to arrange it near the position of the ring.  

Then use the positioning ball to move the component.  

Move to the other side.  
You will see that the current panel has not passed through the ring.  

So we can use the grid comparison tool,  
select all the grids on the back of the small panel,  
then use the positioning ball to move it forward, that is, towards the direction of the screen.  

You can view from the side to see the effect of the ring being created.  

Because the copy simulation involves interaction between the copy and the panel,  
if there is an overlap between the panel and the copy,  
it is recommended to use the select grid tool  
to select the surface area and drag it out.  

Start the simulation,  
and you will see that the ring effect is also created.  

Next, make the twist of the shoulder strap.  

First, turn on the simulation,  
move this shoulder strap panel  
close to the ring component through the fixed pins,  
then turn off the simulation.  

Next, create the shoulder strap twist panel.  

First, use the select grid tool  
to separate the shoulder strap twist panel.  

Then assign this panel  
the shoulder strap fabric.  

At the same time, you can adjust its particle distance  
and collision thickness.  

Add a sewing line,  
then add it to the inside.  

You will see that the panel has now been added to the inside.  

Use the positioning ball  
to adjust the panel inside,  
making it pass through the circular panel.  

Next, you can delete the fixed pins here.  

Note that since the shoulder strap panel is flexible,  
to make the simulation more stable,  
we can freeze this ring  
and adjust the collision thickness of the ring on the right side in the attribute editor.  

For example, change it to 0.5.  
This will reduce the gap between the panels.  

Then turn on the simulation.  

At this point, the panel also passes through the accessory.  

You can use the select grid tool  
to select the passing grids on the panel.  

You can also make a frame selection in the 2D window.  

After selection, adjust its position in the 3D window,  
then turn on the simulation.  

In this way, the panel flips,  
and the ring effect is created.  

Because the shoulder strap should be a complete panel,  
you can merge them into a complete panel.  

Here,  
you can delete this sewing line.  

Then turn on the simulation, then turn it off.  

Next, we add the 日字扣 buckle.  

We can select the attached hardware accessory in the accessory library,  
insert this 日字扣,  
or download and use the corresponding material in Connect.  

Next, adjust the position of this 日字扣.  

Use the compass in the upper right corner of the positioning ball,  
then move it close to the shoulder strap.  

Adjust the position of the accessory  
to determine the position of the 日字扣.  

You can display the internal lines in the clothing information,  
select "display internal lines,"  
and place the center of the 日字扣 near this internal line.  

To make the accessory lie between the shoulder strap and the panel,  
and to reduce the keyframe size,  
you can adjust its collision thickness.  

To control the position of the keyframe,  
we can also freeze this accessory,  
select it and right-click to freeze.  

Next, use the select grid tool  
to select this internal line,  
double-click to select the grids on this line,  
then use the positioning ball to drag it out.  

In this way, we can see that the panel passes through the 日字扣.  

This part is done.  

Then turn on the simulation  
to check if the panel passes through correctly.  

You can see that it passes here,  
so we can select this part of the grid  
and drag it out.  

Then turn on the simulation,  
and turn it off in time.  

Next,  
we make the effect of the shoulder belt passing through.  

This is the passing effect for this part.  

First,  
you can make a small part of the passing section.  

That is,  
on the left and right sides of this internal line,  
add two internal lines  
to position the passing panel.  

We can select this internal line,  
right-click,  
choose internal line diameter,  
and add a 5 mm internal line on both sides.  

This is also the width of the passing panel section.  

Click to confirm.  

Then use the select grid tool  
to select these lines,  
right-click and select "convert to panel."  

Adjust the fabric of the panel,  
its particle distance,  
and collision thickness.  

Sew this panel to the inside of the shoulder belt,  
then add it to the inside.  

Here you will find  
the center of the current panel has not passed through this 日字扣,  
so we still need to do it again.  

Use the select grid tool,  
select the grid in the middle of the panel,  
then push it inward.  

Select the grid in the middle of the panel again,  
and push it inward,  
making it pass through the middle of the 日字扣.  

After adjustment,  
we can sew this panel together with one end of the shoulder belt.  

Move the panel to the top,  
then delete its original sewing line,  

because these two sewing lines  
help us create the buckle.  

Next, add a 10 mm internal line to the panel  
to facilitate sewing.  

Set the distance to 10,  
click to confirm.  

Add the sewing line,  
then turn on the simulation.  

You can see  
this buckle effect is completed.  

Then you can delete one of the sewing lines,  
making it a single complete shoulder belt.  

We need to merge them together,  
mesh them as one.  

If re-simulating, you can see  
the inner shoulder buckle effect clearly.  

If the view is blocked,  
you can use the Select Browse tool to adjust the position.  

Click in the 3D window to locate it,  
then select the blocked part,  
and adjust its position in the 3D window.  

That's all.  

This is the effect of passing through the buckle.

chunks.title: CLO Technique Mini-Class - Adjusting the Strap Through a D-Ring Buckle
chunks.content: ## Overview of CLO Strap Adjustment Using a 日字扣 (Ri Zi Buckle) This section explains how to create and simulate a shoulder strap with an adjustable buckle, specifically the 日字扣 (Ri Zi buckle), in CLO 3D. It focuses on the technical steps to achieve realistic strap adjustment effects through CPU simulation, fabric manipulation, accessory placement, and sewing techniques. --- ## Preparing the Shoulder Strap and Setting Up CPU Simulation This section covers the initial preparation of the shoulder strap panel, including removing fixed sewing lines, twisting the strap, and enabling CPU simulation for realistic interaction between the strap and buckle accessory. - When creating 3D clothing, straps such as shoulder straps on underwear often require an adjustable buckle called a 日字扣 (Ri Zi buckle). - The right side of the underwear example uses this buckle effect, whereas the left side has the strap sewn directly. - To simulate the buckle effect realistically, switch the simulation mode to CPU as the accessory interaction only supports CPU simulation. - Start with the left shoulder strap panel: - Delete the sewing line between shoulder strap parts. - Use the hook and loop tool to attach the shoulder strap onto itself to create a twist. - Adjust fabric properties such as particle distance and collision thickness for the shoulder strap. - Re-add sewing lines and assign the panel to the inside layer. - Add fixed pins along one side of the panel to prevent misalignment during simulation. - Begin simulation to verify initial strap behavior. --- ## Adding and Positioning the Ring Component This section details the steps to insert the ring accessory from the CLO accessory library and position it correctly in relation to the shoulder strap. - Access the accessory library and locate the ring component, or search for it via Connect. - Copy the ring component from the current project file and drag it into the 3D window. - Use the component’s positioning controls (positioning ball and compass) to place the ring near the intended strap location. - Use the grid comparison tool to select the grids on the back of the shoulder strap panel and move them forward so the strap passes through the ring. - View the placement from the side to ensure the strap passes correctly through the ring. - Use the select grid tool to adjust any overlapping areas by dragging surfaces outwards. - Run the simulation to create the interaction effect between the strap and ring. --- ## Creating the Shoulder Strap Twist Panel This section explains how to create a separate twist panel for the shoulder strap that passes through the ring, enhancing realism. - Turn on simulation and move the shoulder strap panel close to the ring using fixed pins; then turn off simulation. - Use the select grid tool to isolate the twist panel section of the shoulder strap. - Assign the appropriate shoulder strap fabric to this new panel. - Adjust particle distance and collision thickness to match the strap.

chunks.title: CLO Technique Mini-Class - Adjusting the Strap Through a D-Ring Buckle
chunks.content: --- ## Creating the Shoulder Strap Twist Panel This section explains how to create a separate twist panel for the shoulder strap that passes through the ring, enhancing realism. - Turn on simulation and move the shoulder strap panel close to the ring using fixed pins; then turn off simulation. - Use the select grid tool to isolate the twist panel section of the shoulder strap. - Assign the appropriate shoulder strap fabric to this new panel. - Adjust particle distance and collision thickness to match the strap. - Add sewing lines and assign this panel to the inside layer. - Use the positioning ball to adjust the twist panel so it passes through the circular ring component. - Remove the fixed pins used earlier to stabilize the simulation. - Freeze the ring accessory and adjust its collision thickness (e.g., set to 0.5) to reduce gaps and improve simulation stability. - Restart simulation and adjust the twist panel grids as needed by selecting and repositioning in 3D, then continue simulation. - Merge the twist panel back into a complete shoulder strap panel by deleting the sewing line between them. - Run simulation to verify the strap behaves as a single, continuous panel. --- ## Inserting and Positioning the 日字扣 (Ri Zi Buckle) Accessory This section describes adding the actual buckle hardware, positioning it accurately, and ensuring the strap passes through it correctly. - Select the 日字扣 buckle from the accessory library or download it via Connect. - Insert the buckle accessory into the 3D scene. - Use the positioning ball’s compass to move and rotate the buckle close to the shoulder strap. - Enable "display internal lines" in clothing information to see internal garment lines. - Align the buckle’s center near an internal line representing the strap’s center. - Adjust the buckle’s collision thickness to help it rest between the strap and the panel, minimizing keyframe size. - Freeze the buckle accessory to fix its position during simulation. - Select the internal line grids on the strap corresponding to the buckle location and drag them through the buckle to simulate passing. - Run simulation to verify the strap passes properly through the buckle. - Adjust and reposition grids as needed to perfect the fit. --- ## Creating the Passing Panel for the Shoulder Strap Through the Buckle This section explains how to create a small passing panel section on the strap that fits through the buckle, including adding internal lines, adjusting dimensions, and sewing. - Add two internal lines on either side of the buckle’s internal center line to define the passing panel's width (5 mm on each side). - Select these internal lines and convert them into a separate panel. - Adjust the fabric properties of this passing panel (particle distance, collision thickness). - Sew the passing panel to the inside of the shoulder strap and assign it to the inside layer.
chunks.content_description: CLO technical experts guide you to use attachments to simulate the real adjustment belt with a Japanese-style buckle effect, suitable for any garment design.

chunks.title: CLO Technique Mini-Class - Adjusting the Strap Through a D-Ring Buckle
chunks.content: --- ## Creating the Passing Panel for the Shoulder Strap Through the Buckle This section explains how to create a small passing panel section on the strap that fits through the buckle, including adding internal lines, adjusting dimensions, and sewing. - Add two internal lines on either side of the buckle’s internal center line to define the passing panel's width (5 mm on each side). - Select these internal lines and convert them into a separate panel. - Adjust the fabric properties of this passing panel (particle distance, collision thickness). - Sew the passing panel to the inside of the shoulder strap and assign it to the inside layer. - The center of this panel may not fully pass through the buckle initially; use the select grid tool to push the middle grids inward through the buckle. - Sew the passing panel to one end of the shoulder strap. - Move the panel to the top layer and delete the original sewing line to allow flexibility. - Add a 10 mm internal line to the panel edge for easier sewing. - Add the sewing line and run simulation. - Verify the buckle effect is created with the panel passing through the buckle. - Delete one of the sewing lines to create a single continuous shoulder strap. - Merge panels to mesh them into one complete panel. - Re-simulate to confirm the inner shoulder buckle effect is visually clear. - If the view is blocked by overlapping geometry, use the Select Browse tool to locate and adjust blocked parts in the 3D window. --- ## Summary of the Final Effect The final result is a realistic shoulder strap wearing the 日字扣 buckle with a natural passing effect through the ring and buckle accessories. The strap is a single continuous panel with appropriate twisting, bending, and fabric collision properties, allowing it to be worn all day with visual realism in CLO 3D simulation.
